per_column.name: writing_plot_issue
per_column.rationale: Provides a strong categorical axis directly answering why audiences are dissatisfied, enabling grouping of complaints by writing failure type. Grounding is mostly sound: 'poor_dialogue' for IMDB-0001 (stilted dialogue, insipid writing) and 'not_present' for the positive review IMDB-0004 are well-warranted. However IMDB-0002 is labeled 'weak_plot' though the sample text criticizes the film generally and cats imagery, not plot specifically, and IMDB-0003 as 'weak_plot' overlaps with performance/premise complaints rather than plot per se, so some categorizations are loosely supported.

per_column.name: emotional_response_failure
per_column.rationale: A genuinely distinct axis from writing issues, useful for modeling a different dimension of dissatisfaction (emotional engagement). Some values are well-grounded: 'not_present' for IMDB-0001 and the positive IMDB-0004. But IMDB-0003 'unbelievable_motivation' is only weakly supported by the 'wooden performances'/'poignant' complaint, and IMDB-0005 'fails_to_move_audience' contradicts a positive review (label_pos=1) that explicitly describes heartache and frustration in an engaged way, an unwarranted reading.

judge.rationale: Both added columns give real, complementary analytical leverage for the query 'why are IMDB audiences dissatisfied?', decomposing complaints into writing/plot failures and emotional-engagement failures — distinct groupable axes, not redundant with the raw review_text or label. Values are largely sound readings of the source text, with correct 'not_present' handling of silent/positive rows. Groundedness is dragged down modestly by several stretched or contradictory assignments (e.g., 'fails_to_move_audience' applied to an engaged positive review), indicating occasional over-confident inference beyond what the text supports.
